replica_rule: replica r: numpy default_rng(r) bootstrap of the 30 train files (counts in the closed form; theta on the first n_sub distinct drawn files); validation and test fixed
title: Architecture A at larger memory and DBP + off-axis triplets
question: Does architecture A close the gap to DBP with larger memory (M = 11, 15; N_c = 31, 63), and do off-axis triplets added to DBP help where the axial ones of E038 duplicated its Kerr phase?

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: decides between A and DBP + off-axis as the reference below ~2.5k RM
value_filter.cheaper_without_training: part 1 yes (closed form); part 2 needs training

decision_if_positive: the winner becomes the reference in E043-type summaries at its RM
decision_if_negative: DBP stays the reference below ~2.5k RM; A is reported as better than plain triplets only
kerr_rm_note: N_c is the total number of phase taps (j = -(N_c - 1)/2 .. (N_c - 1)/2), symmetric alpha: (N_c + 1)/2 distinct weights; Kerr RM = 4 L + 2 + (N_c + 1)/2 + 4 (N_c = 31: 50 RM, N_c = 63: 66 RM); exp from a table (repository convention, as macs_phys)
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
tuning_budget_note: A and triplets-only: closed form, the same 6 lambda values and the same K / K_th sweeps (A has more (M, N_c) combinations); DBP + off-axis: the E025 recipes F6 / F7 as E038 (same budget as E038)

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.a_wins: as E046: A beats triplets-only and Kerr-only at equal RM by > 2 std
rule_draft.offaxis_adds: off-axis triplets add to DBP if (DBP + K off-axis) - DBP alone >= 1 p.p. with non-overlapping intervals (as E038)
rule_draft.a_vs_dbp: A beats DBP + off-axis at an RM level if its test mean is higher by > 2 std (the larger std of the two)
